properties.name: BL-160: a registered checksum's LENGTH is a dialect too, and the compensation lived in the wrong layer. reflow2's own designs register `hexdigest()[:16]` (build_design_graph.py) while an honest caller running `sha256sum` supplies all 64, and `reconcile_artifacts` compared STRINGS — so a full sweep of a provably clean tree reported 51 phantom drifts in the same minute `reflow2_check.py` said "OK — design and build agree". The gate was right for the wrong reason: it carried a Python workaround truncating the observation to the registered length, which no other consumer had. This is BL-125 in a second form and takes the same verdict — a false red on a gate whose whole job is to be believed is worse than no gate. `artifact::checksums_agree` now answers it in the core for every consumer, on BOTH the drift comparison and `set_artifact_checksum`'s would-move-the-baseline guard (the half that would have failed a BL-157 bulk sweep on every short-registered artifact), and the Python workaround is DELETED rather than duplicated by the next consumer. Required is a real PREFIX relationship, never truncate-both-to-N, and it applies to the `sha256:` dialect only. MEASURED ON THE REAL DESIGN: 109 artifacts, 51 truncated baselines, all 51 now unchanged, and the only 4 drifts are the files this change edited. Corrects a belief the design itself had recorded — chg:accept-e52b527aba651ac4 says a full-length registration is "harmless, since reconcile truncates the observation to the registered dialect"; reconcile never did, the gate did.
